This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Windsor Johnston. Former President Barack Obama will hit
the campaign trail in Michigan today to rally support for Democrats ahead of the November
midterms. Michigan Public Radio's Colin Jackson reports his visit coincides with the start of
early in-person voting statewide. As have been on Michigan all election cycle, thanks in part to
its neck-and-neck U.S. Senate race, Republican Mike Rogers has been trying to chip away at
Democrat Abdul El Sayed's base by targeting black voters, especially in Detroit. Strategist Alexis
Wiley says the most important thing Obama can do in Detroit this weekend is show unequivocal support
for El Sayed. Having President Obama's seal of approval is a huge deal and it's going to go a
long way for Abdul. He's going to benefit the most from this weekend. Both major parties see Michigan's
open Senate seat as must win on the path to a majority. Republicans get their own star power
boost Sunday with a visit from President Donald Trump. For NPR News, I'm Colin Jackson. Today
is the last chance to register to vote in the midterms in some states. NPR's Hansi Lo Wang has
a list of the upcoming deadlines. The window is closing today for eligible voters in Massachusetts
and New York to register or update their registration. And we are now one week away
from Halloween on October 31st, which is also the last day in North Carolina for signing up
in person at the state's early voting sites. The only state where voter registration is not required
is North Dakota. And many states allow for same day registration at the polls on November 3rd's
election day. If you're already registered, election officials recommend going to your state's
official election website to confirm your status and contact information before the deadline.
Voters can be removed from lists, especially if they've recently moved, changed their name,
or haven't voted in a while. Hansi Lo Wang, NPR News. The Ukrainian government says
its satellite Internet service is operating at normal speed. NPR's Polina Litnova reports
restrictions with the Starlink communication system had disrupted military drone operations.
Starlink is crucial for Ukraine's military operations and defending against Russian airstrikes.
Last week, without warning, the country lost the ability to use Starlink for these critical
functions. And now Ukraine is seeking alternative satellite communications. President Volodymer
Zelensky announced Ukraine and Finland agreed that Finnish tech giants Nokia and
Isai will help Ukraine to strengthen its satellite capabilities. Polina Litnova, NPR News.
The Trump administration had faced increasing pressure to expand Ukraine's access to
star-shield satellite systems. In a letter to the Pentagon, a bipartisan group of House and Senate
lawmakers urged the White House to lift any speed restrictions related to the systems.
This is NPR News in Washington. The Milwaukee Brewers beat the Tampa Bay Rays
3-1 at home last night in Game 1 of the World Series. NPR's Henry Larson reports fans in
Wisconsin are hoping the Brewers can turn that win into the team's first championship.
It's been 44 years since the Brewers had a shot like this, and devotees packed into Stenny's,
a Milwaukee institution that runs a regular shuttle between the bar and the ball field.
I've been telling folks for the last month and a half something different this year.
I was there for 82. I'm here now. Wayne Cregett has been enamored with Milwaukee baseball since
he was five years old listening to the radio. He didn't get a ticket. Those are going for
thousands of dollars online. But what he lacks in first base seats, he makes up for in total
confidence. They're going to win it their way. Whether it's in five, six, seven, four,
doesn't matter. Cregett says he'll be ready when the Brewers get their next shot at making history
Saturday night. Henry Larson, NPR News, Milwaukee. Major League Baseball could face a lockout
beginning December 2nd as team owners push for a salary cap. The Players Union says it will never
accept one, raising the prospect of a work stoppage that could cancel games next season.
The league argues a cap would make teams more competitive. This year's World Series is the first
since 1991, featuring two teams in the bottom half of league payrolls. I'm Windsor Johnston, NPR News,
in Washington. This message comes from IXL. With IXL, you get personalized online learning and
